newsitem.title: ITALY: Bulk of Italy force to go to Albania from Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Bulk of Italy force to go to Albania from Tuesday.

text.p: The bulk of the Italian force which will spearhead a multinational security mission in Albania will start moving to the small Balkan state from Tuesday, Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Saturday.
Prodi told parliament a small contingent of Italian soldiers was already in Albania, but the main force would be deployed from April 15.

"Even if some of our soldiers are already in Albania, the main structure of our mission will leave on Tuesday and over the following 10 days," Prodi said, adding that he wanted to set up a parliamentary committee to monitor the mission.
Officials had indicated earlier that the Italian force was expected to be deployed from Monday onwards.
The bulk of the 6,000-strong force, the first of its kind to be led by Italy, will be deployed next week in a mission sanctioned by the United Nations to protect the delivery of aid supplies.

Albania plunged into near-anarchy last month amid popular anger over the collapse of get-rich-quick investment schemes. Local media said on Saturday that 279 people had been killed in unrest since March 1, not including an estimated 80 who died in the sinking of a refugee boat.
Italy has commited about 2,500 troops to the operation, with an advance party of 20 men arriving in the western Albanian port of Durres on Friday.

Italian Defence Minister Beniamino Andreatta and Defence Chief of Staff Guido Venturoni, who has overall command of the mission, would fly to Tirana on Saturday for political meetings ahead of the deployment, defence sources said.
Two Italian military aircraft continued airlifts of equipment to Tirana on Saturday to prepare the way for the arrival of the multinational force.

Troops from France, Greece, Spain, Turkey and Romania are also in the force, which is being organised by a so-called coalition of willing nations. Austria and Denmark are also considering participation.
A French naval vessel with around 120 men aboard was expected to leave the Italian port of Brindisi this weekend for a reconnaisance mission in Durres.
"We are waiting for our orders to depart and go to Durres," said French Major Herve Gourmelon. "I would like to know the date as well. It could be this evening or tomorrow," he added.
Two Spanish naval ships were due to arrive in Brindisi on Sunday.

Italy had suggested Portugal would contribute but the country's Defence Minister Antonio Vitorino was quoted on Thursday as saying no soldiers would go because the conditions were not right and the risks were too great.

Prodi, who won parliamentary backing for the mission on Wednesday but at the cost of a split with his hard-left allies, said on Saturday he hoped "elections (in Albania) will happen quickly and that one month after the vote we can begin to bring our troops back."
The wave of unrest has forced Albanian President Sali Berisha to call a general election by the end of June.
